resolutions.researcher_notes: Status 'operating' is inferred from context, not stated for this specific parallel line. Zawya (Aramco says Haradh and Hawiyah gas fields fully onstream in 2023) confirms the Haradh/Hawiyah Khuff gas system is producing; Saudipedia confirms the Hawiyah Gas Plant is operating and processing al-Khuff sour gas. Both are independent of GEM. No source names 'Haradh Khuff-Hawiyah 2' as a distinct segment; the three GEM entries (P1918 and siblings) are undifferentiated parallel lines.

Fuel=Gas is well supported: offshore-technology's Haradh project profile describes Khuff gas transmission lines and Saudi Aramco gas trains; Saudipedia describes the Hawiyah Gas Plant processing sour gas from the al-Khuff and al-Jawf reservoirs. Two independent editorial sources agree the Haradh->Hawiyah system carries (Khuff) gas.

No independent source states a 43 km length for this line. The '43 km / 27 miles' figure appears only on GEM pages and search-engine summaries that restate GEM (offshore-technology's GlobalData 'Haradh-Hawiyah Gas' data card gives an unrelated 450 km / 36 in for a different asset). The only GEM-cited source is OPEC ASB 2012 p.75, a statistics bulletin that does not give per-pipeline length. Not fabricating a URL; marking UNRESOLVED.

Circumstantial support only: offshore-technology's Haradh profile states the field's Khuff gas is carried by 'five 20in and 30in gas transmission' lines totalling 130 km, so 30-inch is the diameter class used for Haradh Khuff gas transmission. It does NOT segment-confirm 30 in for this specific 43 km Haradh->Hawiyah line (those 130 km lines feed the Haradh plant, not the Hawiyah plant). No independent source confirms the exact 30-inch spec of P1918; treat as weak/partial.

StartCountryOrArea/EndCountryOrArea='Saudi Arabia' and EndLocation='Al Hawiyah' are supported: Saudipedia and offshore-technology place both the Haradh field and the Hawiyah Gas Plant in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province (Haradh ~280 km SW of Dhahran in the southern Ghawar field; Hawiyah plant near Al-Jubail / Ghawar). CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: GEM's EndState/Province='Makkah' is wrong — the Hawiyah Gas Plant is in the Eastern Province, not Makkah. GEM likely conflated it with the separate Makkah-region 'Al Hawiyah' (the Madrakah-Al Hawiyah pipeline). Recommend correcting EndState/Province to Eastern Province.

Owner1='Saudi Aramco' 100% is strongly supported: offshore-technology states Saudi Aramco operates the Haradh natural gas and oil development; Saudipedia states Saudi Aramco operates the Hawiyah Gas Plant as part of its Master Gas System. Two independent sources; consistent with Aramco's wholly state-owned status. No third-party or joint owner indicated.
